design_rationale: The study is a pragmatic, two-arm, open randomised controlled trial where participants were assigned to intervention arms using independent web-based computer-generated randomisation with minimisation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was computer-generated and concealed via an independent central web-based system, and baseline characteristics were balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Three hundred and twenty children were randomised, 160 to each group, using independent web-based computer-generated randomisation (with minimisation based on age, sex and baseline severity of OME) to either nasal balloon autoinflation performed three times per day for 1 – 3 months plus usual care, or usual care alone.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the study was open-label due to the nature of the medical device, analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle with no indication of non-protocol deviations that would bias the objective tympanometry outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Owing to the nature of the intervention use of placebo was not possible, and therefore nurses, children and families were unable to be masked to treatment allocation. [...] Analysis was by intention to treat (ITT) and per protocol (PP) according to an analysis plan.

domain_judgments.rationale: Retention was high and balanced between groups across follow-up time points, and sensitivity analyses using multiple imputation showed robust results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At 1 month, the proportion of children with normal tympanograms was 47.3% (62/131) in those allocated to autoinflation and 35.6% (47/132) in those receiving usual care [...] At 3 months, the proportions were 49.6% (62/125) and 38.3% (46/120), respectively [...] Sensitivity analyses using multiple imputations and a PP population analysis showed no significant differences between groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome of tympanometric resolution is an objective physiological measure, and assessments were anonymized and graded by an expert panel blinded to treatment allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The proportion of children demonstrating clearance of middle ear fluid in at least one ear (with normal tympanograms) at 1 and 3 months, assessed blind to treatment. [...] Tympanometry outcomes at 1 and 3 months were anonymised by the Primary Care and Vaccines Collaborative Clinical Trials Unit and assessed blind by an expert panel.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered prospectively (ISRCTN55208702) and reported analyses adhered to a pre-specified statistical analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Analysis was by intention to treat (ITT) and per protocol (PP) according to an analysis plan. [...] The primary aim was to evaluate the clinical effectiveness of autoinflation in resolving OME at 1 and 3 months by assessing the proportions of children showing rigorously defined improvement, that is, tympanometric resolution of at least one type B tympanogram (fluid) ear per child back to normal pressures A/C1 types.

overall_summary: The trial was well conducted with robust central web-based randomization, blinded expert evaluation of an objective primary outcome (tympanometry), low and balanced attrition, and analysis following a pre-specified protocol. All five domains were judged to be at low risk of bias.

design_rationale: Subjects were stratified by their ability to achieve tubal opening and then randomly assigned to either the autoinflation or control group using a set of random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: While a random sequence was generated using a set of random numbers, there is no information provided regarding allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Within each stratification, subjects were randomly assigned to either the autoinflation or the control group by the use of a set of random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the trial was unblinded due to the nature of the device intervention, control participants were prevented from cross-over and compliance was monitored without important unintended deviations from protocol.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All subjects were exposed to the method of autoinflation during the testing session. To keep the subjects in the control group and their parents from attempting autoinflation at home during the study, they were assured at the onset of the study that all subjects would have the opportunity to use the autoinflation system at the completion of the study... None of the subjects in the control group reported attempting autoinflation during the study period.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 1 of 41 enrolled subjects withdrew after entry, leaving 40 of 41 (97.6%) available for evaluation at the 2-week primary endpoint.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 41 subjects who were entered, 38 (92.7 percent) were available for evaluation at the one-week endpoint; one subject in the control group withdrew from the study after entry and one subject from each of the two study groups failed to return for the one-week visit, but both of these children were evaluated at the two-week endpoint.

domain_judgments.rationale: The otoscopic and tympanometric outcome assessments were performed by an investigator without mention of blinding to group assignment, introducing potential observer bias for the clinical otoscopic component.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The diagnosis of OME was based on the findings of one of the authors (K.H.C.), who is a 'validated otoscopist' (sensitivity = 82%; specificity = 89%)... All subjects received an otologic examination and tympanogram at each of the two weekly follow-up visits.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome and analysis were reported consistently as pre-specified for all evaluated participants, with no indication of selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The proportions of children who were effusion-free at 2 weeks were compared in the two study groups by use of the Fisher's exact test.

overall_summary: The overall judgment is some concerns, driven by the lack of information regarding allocation concealment in Domain 1 and unblinded clinical otoscopic outcome assessment in Domain 4.

design_rationale: The study states that 100 children were consecutively randomized to either autoinflation or a control observation group.

domain_judgments.rationale: The method of sequence generation and allocation concealment is not reported, although baseline characteristics were comparable.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: One hundred children were consecutively randomized to undergo either autoinflation, using a new device, or placed in a control group.

domain_judgments.rationale: The authors explicitly excluded non-compliant participants from the comparative analyses, violating intention-to-treat and introducing potential bias due to adherence selection.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Comparison of the two groups included only those children who had performed autoinflation as prescribed.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were lost to follow-up over subsequent visits (decreasing from 73 to 49 ears in control and 51 to 42 in intervention by day 90) with reasons for attrition not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 50 children randomized to the autoinflation group, 20 girls and 26 boys (median age, 5.3 years) attended, as a minimum, the first three trials... Of the 50 children in the control group, 19 girls and 28 boys (median age, 5.3 years) attended at least the three first trials.

domain_judgments.rationale: Tympanometry is an objective physiological measurement of middle ear pressure unlikely to be influenced by lack of blinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Otomicroscopy and tympanometry were performed after 2 weeks (at visit 3), after 1 month (visit 4), after 2 months (visit 5), and after 3 months (visit 6).

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration or pre-specified analysis protocol is available, and results are reported using post-hoc ear-level subgroupings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Statistical analysis was performed using the Mann-Whitney rank sum test. The chosen level of significance was P<.05.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high due to Domain 2, as the primary comparative effectiveness analysis excluded participants who did not adhere to the autoinflation protocol rather than analyzing on an intention-to-treat basis. Additional concerns exist regarding allocation concealment and incomplete outcome reporting across follow-up visits.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated using a centralized web-based computer-generated randomization service with minimization.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence generation and concealment were ensured through an independent web-based computerized system with minimization, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: An independent external agency provided a centralized Web-based computer-generated randomization system (www.sealedenvelope.com) for nurses to access while recruiting children. ... The randomization involved an algorithm with minimization based on 3 variables: age, sex and baseline severity (bilateral v. unilateral type-B tympanograms).

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the trial was open-label due to the nature of the device, there was no indication of unintended deviations from protocol, and an intention-to-treat approach was used for the analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Because of the nature of the intervention, use of placebo was not possible, and therefore nurses, children and families were not masked to treatment allocation. ... We performed a modified intention-to-treat analysis, ignoring reported compliance but excluding children for whom no outcome measurement could be made.

domain_judgments.rationale: Missing outcome data were low, balanced between groups with similar reasons, and sensitivity analyses using multiple imputation yielded consistent findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Retention was good, with 8.4% lost to follow-up at 1 month and 12.2% at 3 months. Uninterpretable tympanograms due to poor technique (leakage or low canal volume), and clinical problems (wax or perforation) were similar between groups, leaving 131 children in the autoinflation arm and 132 in the usual care arm in the modified intention-to-treat analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was an objective measurement (tympanometry) evaluated by blinded experts reviewing anonymized printouts, preventing influence by knowledge of intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Two members of the trial team, trained in tympanometry and masked to allocation, independently reviewed anonymized tympanometry printouts. The expert interrater agreement was 89%, and disagreement was settled by a third independent audiologist.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, an analysis protocol was prespecified, and outcomes were reported in accordance with the planned analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Analyses were conducted using SAS version 9.3 and Stata version 13.0 according to a prespecified analysis plan. Trial registration: ISRCTN, No. 55208702.

overall_summary: The study is at low risk of bias across all RoB 2 domains, featuring robust centralized randomization, masked outcome assessment for the objective primary outcome, low balanced attrition, and analysis according to a prespecified protocol.

design_rationale: The authors explicitly state that participants were randomly divided into two groups (autoinflation vs. control).

domain_judgments.rationale: The study states participants were randomly divided into groups, but provides no details on sequence generation or allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients were randomly divided into two groups: Group 1 (autoinflation); treated with autoinflation three times a day for 6 weeks (Otovent®), with nasal saline irrigation 3 times a day for 6 weeks, and group 2 (control); treated with only nasal saline irrigation 3 times a day for 6 weeks.

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding was not possible given the nature of the device, but deviations from the intended intervention were minor, balanced, and an appropriate analysis aligned with assignment was performed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The compliance of the children to the autoinflation was satisfactory and the autoinflation was somehow amusing for the children. Eleven children who had upper respiratory tract infection ceased the autoinflation for 5 days but autoinflation treatment was completed to 6 weeks.

domain_judgments.rationale: Loss to follow-up was relatively low (around 11-12% of ears) and similar between the two groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: During the 9 months follow-up, in autoinflation group; 20 out of 48 ears (42%) required the ventilation tube insertion, 22 ears (46 %) were free of effusion, and 6 ears (12%) were lost in follow-up and in control group; 30 out of 45 ears (67%) required the insertion of ventilation tube, 8 ears (17.7 %) were free of effusion, 5 ears (11%) were lost in follow-up, and 2 ears of 1 patient who regretted the insertion of ventilation tube had still COME.

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcome assessors were not reported as blinded, and the decision to insert ventilation tubes or evaluate effusion with pneumatic otoscopy involves clinical judgment that could be influenced by knowledge of intervention status.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients in both groups were examined with pneumatic otoscopy and tympanogram once every two weeks for the first two months and then once a month for 7 months.

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-trial registration or published statistical analysis plan was provided, raising some concerns regarding potential selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Recovery rates of effusions in both groups in the 6th week, 3rd month, 6th month, and 9th month follow-up were shown in table 3... Insertion of ventilation tube in both groups in the 3rd month, 6th month, and 9th month follow-up was shown in Table 4.

overall_summary: The study is judged to have some concerns overall due to insufficient reporting of sequence generation and allocation concealment, lack of blinding of outcome assessors for clinical evaluations and ventilation tube decisions, and absence of a pre-registered protocol.

design_rationale: The authors state that children were 'allocated at random into two groups' to receive either autoinflation or no treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although participants were described as 'allocated at random', no details are provided regarding sequence generation or allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The children so selected were, with the informed consent of their parents, allocated at random into two groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial compared autoinflation to no treatment; parents reported good compliance and there is no evidence of unintended deviations or failure to follow assigned groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Group A children were asked to inflate a balloon nasally 3 times daily while Group B were untreated.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for all 40 children and all 78 glue ears randomized, indicating no missing outcome data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Twenty-one children with a total of 41 glue ears were allocated to Group A and 19 children with 37 glue ears were allocated to Group B... In Group A, of the 41 ears investigated 37 showed no improvement... In Group B, of the 37 ears investigated, 27 showed no improvement.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study does not state whether outcome assessors (performing otoscopy and audiometry/tympanometry) were blinded to the intervention group, and otoscopy/audiometry involve subjective judgment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The children were reviewed after 3 weeks and had repeat otoscopy, pure tone audiogram and tympanogram.

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no indication of a pre-registered trial protocol or analysis plan, and reported results include post hoc composite improvement definitions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The ear was considered to have improved if: (1) There was an average improvement of 10 dB in the pure tone audiogram frequencies from 250–2000 Hz. (2) A peak appeared in a previously flat tympanogram.

overall_summary: The study is judged to have some concerns overall due to insufficient reporting of the random sequence generation and allocation concealment methods, unblinded outcome assessment, and absence of a pre-registered protocol.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that participants were randomly allocated to study groups using computer-generated, independent allocation sequences in blocks of six.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although computer-generated sequence generation was used, allocation concealment is unclear ('assigned to group A or B by one of the authors'), and there was a statistically significant baseline imbalance in age (p=0.004) and hearing threshold (p=0.016).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Computer-generated, independent allocation sequences were used for randomisation. To avoid disproportionate numbers of patients in each group, randomisation was performed in blocks of six subjects... The children were enrolled by a secretary and assigned to group A or B by one of the authors (ABM)... There was a difference between the groups regarding age (p = 0.004) and hearing thresholds for the best hearing ear (p = 0.016) at entry.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and parents were aware of the assigned intervention (autoinflation device vs. control/observation in period 1), and while analysis included all enrolled children or handled crossover, the unblinded nature of behavioral treatment and subjective encouragement may have introduced deviations from intended protocol.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The parents and the children received written, verbal and visual (video) instructions on how to use the device... In one case, the compliance was not satisfactory to complete the four-week treatment... The main analysis was defined as treatment effect adjusted by the control effect.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data for the primary trial period (first four and eight weeks) were available for all 45 randomized children.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Characteristics at entry of the 45 evaluable subjects... After eight weeks after treatment in both groups, based on the tympanometric, audiometric and otomicroscopic findings four of 45 children were submitted to grommet surgery.

domain_judgments.rationale: Audiometry was conducted by an assessor blinded to group allocation, and tympanometry is an objective physiological measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Pure tone air conduction thresholds for each ear or sound field audiometry for both ears were performed by an experienced audiologist who was blinded to the group allocation of the child... The tympanometric equipment used in the study was a Grason–Stadler GSI 33... Middle-Ear Analyser...

domain_judgments.rationale: No prospective trial registration or pre-specified statistical analysis plan is referenced, and analytical choices (e.g. non-standard crossover adjustments and multiple subgroup/ear-level metrics) raise some concerns for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome measurements were improvement in middle-ear pressure and hearing thresholds at eight weeks... Conventional cross-over analysis was not performed due to expected carry-over effect after the treatment period... The main analysis was defined as treatment effect adjusted by the control effect.

overall_summary: The study has some concerns overall, driven by potential issues with allocation concealment and baseline imbalances in age and hearing thresholds (Domain 1), open-label intervention deviations (Domain 2), and absence of a pre-registered trial protocol specifying the analysis of the cross-over design (Domain 5).
